### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every trace ran the consecutive chain A24 → A25 → A26: all observed outgoing transitions of A24 went to A25 and all of those of A25 went to A26, with A24–A25 and A25–A26 always exactly one step apart and A24–A26 always two steps apart. [DIR006, DIR007, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
- The five activities A14, A15, A20, A21 and A22 appear in none of the 200 earlier traces. In the later window each occurs in about 17–23 of 100 traces (A14 in 45, A15 in 42, A20 in 44, A21 in 33, A22 in 35 of 200), at most once per trace, around the middle of the trace (mean relative position about 0.5). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004]
- The five are mutually exclusive as far as observed: no tested pair among A14, A15, A20 and A21 ever occurs in the same trace, and their combined participation of 199 of 200 traces matches the share of later traces in which the A24–A26 distance is three steps instead of the previous two. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL007, REL008, REL012, LAG002]
- Routing around the new step changed: in the later window A24 leads directly to A25 in about 49 of 100 of its outgoing transitions (previously all of them) and to one of the five new activities in about 51 of 100; A25 leads directly to A26 in about 52 of 100 (previously all) and to one of the five in about 48 of 100. Accordingly, the direct pairs A24–A25 and A25–A26 are one step apart in only about half of the later traces. [DIR006, DIR007, LAG001, LAG003]
- Each new activity leads to A25 or to A26 in roughly equal shares (for A14, about 53 of 100 transitions go to A25 and 47 to A26). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Ordering: a new activity always executes after A24 (A24 first in all 45 traces containing both A24 and A14) and always before A26 (A14 first in all 45 traces containing both), while against A25 both orders occur (A14 before A25 in about 12 of 100 traces, A25 before A14 in about 11 of 100). [REL004, REL005, REL006, REL009, REL011, REL013, REL015]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, a new step with five mutually exclusive variants — A14, A15, A20, A21 and A22 — is executed within the previously fixed sequence A24 → A25 → A26: in roughly half of the traces it sits between A24 and A25, in the other half between A25 and A26, so that A24 and A25 each keep their original direct successor in only about half of the cases. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR006, DIR007, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

The sign is direct and consistent: the five activities rise from absent to about 17–23 of 100 traces, each new activity always follows A24 and precedes A26, with a mixed order against A25 exactly as the two alternative spots predict, and the A24–A26 distance grows from two to three steps in 199 of 200 later traces. Screening tested 89 control-flow units and qualified 34 items, against about 0.44 expected if nothing had changed — a count many times larger than chance — and every qualifying item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1000 random re-splits, so the body of evidence goes far beyond what an unchanged process typically produces. [REL004, REL005, REL006, REL009, REL011, REL013, REL015, LAG002, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL007, REL008, REL012, REL010, REL014, REL009, REL011, REL013, REL015, LAG001, LAG003, screening]

The main competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the five activities already existed before but occurred in fewer than about 1 of 200 traces, since zero participation only means they were not observed in the earlier window; the roughly 52/48 split between the two positions of the new step is likewise a sample estimate from 200 traces. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR006, DIR007]
